observed.title: 38. 机械波的传播

paragraphs.text:
要理解波的传播，就要看清介质中的各个质点怎样运动。
先从沿橡皮绳传播的横波开始，区分质点的局部振动与波沿绳的传播。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
橡皮绳的每一小段都具有质量和弹性。
绳发生形变时，弹力通过各个截面作用于相邻绳段。
作用在绳段上的合回复力趋向于使它回到平衡位置。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
由于惯性，运动中的绳段到达平衡位置时不会立即停下，而会越过这个位置。
继续偏离平衡位置时，回复力使它向外的运动逐渐减慢。
到达最大偏移处时，绳段短暂停下，随后向平衡位置返回。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图69用一串相同的金属球组成的链子来模拟细绳。
各球悬挂在线上，相邻球之间用弹簧连接。
弹簧的质量比球的质量小得多。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
因此，模型的质量主要集中在各球上。
球之间的弹性联系则主要由轻弹簧提供。
把质量和弹性这样分开，仍能说明细绳中波传播的基本机制，但不能据此认为模型与真实细绳的一切细节都相同。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在水平面上，把最左边的球向链线的侧方移离平衡位置。
这里的侧向位移垂直于链线，对应所研究的横向运动。
连接的弹簧发生形变，弹力使第二个球也开始向同一侧运动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
第二个球具有惯性，因此它的响应不是瞬时完成的。
它的运动跟随第一个球的运动，在时间上有所滞后。
这里采用小幅运动的理想模型，并先不考虑明显损耗和反射的影响。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
用手或机械装置使第一个球以周期 $T$ 振动。
第二个球受到弹簧的周期性作用而作受迫振动，相位比第一个球滞后。
第三个球通过下一根弹簧受到作用，振动的相位又进一步滞后。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
扰动就这样沿球链逐个传递。
初始暂态过去后，受驱动的各球以驱动频率振动，而沿传播方向存在相位滞后。
在反射波尚未返回的传播区域内，这种横向振动形成沿球链前进的横波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图70的 a、b、c、d、e、f 六幅俯视图依次记录横波传播时各球的位置，相邻两幅对应的时刻相差四分之一振动周期。
各球旁的箭头表示该球在相应时刻的速度矢量，也就是运动方向和快慢。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图71a所示的弹性模型由重球和连接它们的轻弹簧组成。
球的悬挂方式使它们只能沿链线振动。
沿这个方向使第一个球以周期 $T$ 振动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
纵波便沿球链传播。
球间距离交替变小和变大，形成密集和稀疏的区域。
图71b展示了这种疏密分布，而每个球仍是在自己的局部位置附近往复运动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

observed.title: 38. 机械波的传播

paragraphs.text:
要理解波的传播，就要看清介质中的各个质点怎样运动。
先从沿橡皮绳传播的横波开始，区分质点的局部振动与波沿绳的传播。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
橡皮绳的每一小段都具有质量和弹性。
绳发生形变时，弹力通过各个截面作用于相邻绳段。
作用在绳段上的合回复力趋向于使它回到平衡位置。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
由于惯性，运动中的绳段到达平衡位置时不会立即停下，而会越过这个位置。
继续偏离平衡位置时，回复力使它向外的运动逐渐减慢。
到达最大偏移处时，绳段短暂停下，随后向平衡位置返回。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图69用一串相同的金属球组成的链子来模拟细绳。
各球悬挂在线上，相邻球之间用弹簧连接。
弹簧的质量比球的质量小得多。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
因此，模型的质量主要集中在各球上。
球之间的弹性联系则主要由轻弹簧提供。
把质量和弹性这样分开，仍能说明细绳中波传播的基本机制，但不能据此认为模型与真实细绳的一切细节都相同。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在水平面上，把最左边的球向链线的侧方移离平衡位置。
这里的侧向位移垂直于链线，对应所研究的横向运动。
连接的弹簧发生形变，弹力使第二个球也开始向同一侧运动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
第二个球具有惯性，因此它的响应不是瞬时完成的。
它的运动跟随第一个球的运动，在时间上有所滞后。
这里采用小幅运动的理想模型，并先不考虑明显损耗和反射的影响。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
用手或机械装置使第一个球以周期 $T$ 振动。
第二个球受到弹簧的周期性作用而作受迫振动，相位比第一个球滞后。
第三个球通过下一根弹簧受到作用，振动的相位又进一步滞后。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
扰动就这样沿球链逐个传递。
初始暂态过去后，受驱动的各球以驱动频率振动，而沿传播方向存在相位滞后。
在反射波尚未返回的传播区域内，这种横向振动形成沿球链前进的横波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图70的 a、b、c、d、e、f 六幅俯视图依次记录横波传播时各球的位置，相邻两幅对应的时刻相差四分之一振动周期。
各球旁的箭头表示该球在相应时刻的速度矢量，也就是运动方向和快慢。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图71a所示的弹性模型由重球和连接它们的轻弹簧组成。
球的悬挂方式使它们只能沿链线振动。
沿这个方向使第一个球以周期 $T$ 振动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
纵波便沿球链传播。
球间距离交替变小和变大，形成密集和稀疏的区域。
图71b展示了这种疏密分布，而每个球仍是在自己的局部位置附近往复运动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

observed.title: 38. Wave Propagation

paragraphs.text:
To understand wave propagation, we need to follow individual particles of the medium.
We begin with a transverse wave traveling along an elastic cord.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Every short segment of the cord has both mass and elasticity.
When the cord bends, elastic forces act across its cross sections.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
The net restoring force tends to pull each segment toward equilibrium.
Inertia carries a moving segment past its equilibrium position.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Beyond equilibrium, the restoring force slows its outward motion.
At maximum displacement it stops briefly, then starts back.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Figure 69 models the cord with a chain of identical metal balls.
The balls hang from strings and are joined by springs.
The springs have much less mass than the balls.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Most of the model's mass is concentrated in the balls.
The light springs provide elastic coupling.
This captures the basic wave mechanism, not every detail of a real cord.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Move the leftmost ball sideways in the horizontal plane.
Here, sideways means perpendicular to the chain.
The connecting spring deforms and pulls the second ball sideways.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
That ball has inertia, so its response takes time.
Its motion follows the first ball's motion with a delay.
We use a small-amplitude model, before appreciable loss or reflection.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Drive the first ball periodically with period $T$, by hand or a mechanism.
The second ball is forced to oscillate, with a phase delay.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Through the next spring, the third ball responds with a further delay.
The disturbance continues from ball to ball along the chain.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
After the initial transient, the driven balls share the driving frequency.
Before reflected waves return, this is an outgoing transverse wave.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Figure 70 has six overhead views of the ball positions, labeled a, b, c, d, e, and f.
The views are a quarter-cycle apart, and each arrow is a ball's velocity vector.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Figure 71a uses heavy balls connected by light springs.
The suspension lets each ball oscillate only along the chain.
Drive the first ball with period $T$ along that same direction.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
A longitudinal wave then travels along the chain.
Close and wide gaps between balls form compressions and rarefactions.
Figure 71b shows the pattern as each ball oscillates locally.

texts:
To understand wave propagation, we need to follow individual particles of the medium.
We begin with a transverse wave traveling along an elastic cord.

Every short segment of the cord has both mass and elasticity.
When the cord bends, elastic forces act across its cross sections.

The net restoring force tends to pull each segment toward equilibrium.
Inertia carries a moving segment past its equilibrium position.

Beyond equilibrium, the restoring force slows its outward motion.
At maximum displacement it stops briefly, then starts back.

Figure 69 models the cord with a chain of identical metal balls.
The balls hang from strings and are joined by springs.
The springs have much less mass than the balls.

Most of the model's mass is concentrated in the balls.
The light springs provide elastic coupling.
This captures the basic wave mechanism, not every detail of a real cord.
Figure 69

Move the leftmost ball sideways in the horizontal plane.
Here, sideways means perpendicular to the chain.
The connecting spring deforms and pulls the second ball sideways.

That ball has inertia, so its response takes time.
Its motion follows the first ball's motion with a delay.
We use a small-amplitude model, before appreciable loss or reflection.

Drive the first ball periodically with period $T$, by hand or a mechanism.
The second ball is forced to oscillate, with a phase delay.

Through the next spring, the third ball responds with a further delay.
The disturbance continues from ball to ball along the chain.

After the initial transient, the driven balls share the driving frequency.
Before reflected waves return, this is an outgoing transverse wave.

Figure 70 has six overhead views of the ball positions, labeled a, b, c, d, e, and f.
The views are a quarter-cycle apart, and each arrow is a ball's velocity vector.

Figure 71a uses heavy balls connected by light springs.
The suspension lets each ball oscillate only along the chain.
Drive the first ball with period $T$ along that same direction.

A longitudinal wave then travels along the chain.
Close and wide gaps between balls form compressions and rarefactions.
Figure 71b shows the pattern as each ball oscillates locally.

observed.title: 39. 波长　波速

paragraphs.text:
在横波传播时，当振动传到了第十三个球后，第一个和第十三个球将作完全相同的振动。
当第一个球在平衡位置上并向左运动时（见图70e），第十三个球也在平衡位置，并且也向左运动。
又过了$\frac{1}{4}$周期，第一个球向左运动到最大偏移位置，第十三个球同样也到达这样的位置（见图70f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这两个球的振动相位总是相同的。
**相距最近的振动相位相同的两个点间的距离叫做波长**。
所以，第一个球和第十三个球之间的距离，第二个球和第十四个球之间的距离，第三个球和第十五个球之间的距离都等于波长（见图70e、f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图71b所示纵波的波长等于第二个球与第十四个球之间的距离，或第四个球与第十六个球之间的距离。
波长用希腊字母$\lambda$表示。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在波传播时，物体的不同点（例如这个模型中的各个球），只要它们之间的距离不等于$n\lambda$（$n$为整数），就以不同的相位振动。
相距$\lambda/2$的第一个球和第七个球（见图70）以相反的相位振动：当第一个球向左运动时，第七个球就向右运动，反过来也是这样。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在一个周期内，波传播的距离为$\lambda$（见图70e）。
因此，波速可由下面的公式求出：
$v=\frac{\lambda}{T}$ (4.1)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
因为周期$T$与频率$\nu$的关系为
$T=\frac{1}{\nu}$，
所以：
$v=\lambda\nu$ (4.2)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: **波速等于波长与振动频率的乘积**。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: 波沿绳传播时，我们可以观察到两种周期性。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
第一，绳的每个质点随时间作周期性振动。
在谐振动的情况下，这些振动遵循正弦或余弦规律，各质点的频率和振幅相同，区别仅在于相位。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
第二，在任一时刻，绳上每隔$\lambda$的距离就会出现重复的波形。
图72中过$O$点的曲线表示某一时刻的波形。
随着时间推移，整个波形以速度$v$从左向右移动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
经过一段时间
$\Delta t=\frac{\Delta s}{v}$
波形就变成图中不过$O$点的那条曲线。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: 表示波速、波长与振动频率关系的公式(4.2)，同样适用于纵波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

u}$C. $v=\lambda T=\dfrac{\lambda}{
u}$D. $v=\dfrac{2\lambda}{T}=2\lambda
u$5.在图70中，波已传到的两个相邻球之间，最小相位差的大小是多少弧度？A. $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$B. $\dfrac{2\pi}{13}$C. $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$D. $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

observed.title: 39. 波长　波速 - 书写题与标准答案

blocks.text: 39. 波长　波速 - 书写题与标准答案

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
1. 什么叫做波？机械波是振动或扰动在弹性介质中的传播。一个质点偏离平衡位置后，通过作用力使相邻质点依次振动，扰动便从一处传到另一处。各质点是在各自的局部位置附近振动，并不是跟着波穿过整个介质。2. 横波与纵波有什么区别？分别举出横波与纵波的例子。横波中，介质质点的振动方向与波的传播方向垂直。例如，把拉紧的绳向侧方拨动，扰动沿绳传播，而各绳段沿垂直于传播方向的方向往复运动。

纵波中，介质质点的振动方向与波的传播方向平行。例如，沿弹簧的长度方向来回推拉一端，密集和稀疏的区域便沿弹簧传播。空气中的声波也是纵波：空气质点沿声音的传播方向来回振动。3. 波动的基本特点是什么？波动的基本特点是：扰动和能量能够沿介质传播，却不伴随介质物质的持续整体输运。在本课的理想机械波模型中，各质点只在自己的平衡位置附近往复振动，并不跟着波一起前进。

例如，在球与弹簧组成的链子中，形变的弹簧对下一个球施力并做功，能量通过弹簧从一个球传向下一个球，而各球仍在各自的局部位置附近振动。这并不是说质点没有运动。4. 什么叫做波长？波长 $\lambda$ 是沿波的传播方向，相距最近的两个不同的同相位振动点之间的距离。同相位的点同时重复相同的振动状态，位移和运动方向都相同。如果两个点只在某一瞬间位移相同，但运动方向相反，就不能据此认为它们同相位。

例如，相邻两个波峰之间的距离，或纵波中相邻两个密集区之间的距离，都是一个波长。图70中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔就是一个波长。5. 波速与波长有什么关系？在一个振动周期 $T$ 内，波形向前传播一个波长 $\lambda$，所以波速为 $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$，其中 $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ 是振动频率。也就是说，波速等于波长与频率的乘积。在频率保持不变时，波长越大，波速越大。这里的波速是波的传播速度，不是某个振动质点的瞬时速度。6. 指出图70中两个相邻的球振动的相位差。图70e中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔等于一个波长，其中有12个相等的相邻间隔，所以相邻间隔为 $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$。

对于已经进入振动的两个相邻球，相位差的大小为 $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ 弧度，即 $30^\circ$。沿波的传播方向，后一个球比前一个球滞后十二分之一周期，相应的时间滞后为 $\frac{T}{12}$。相邻两幅图之间的 $\frac{T}{4}$ 是拍下两幅图的时间间隔，不是相邻两球的振动滞后时间。

observed.title: 39. 波长　波速

paragraphs.text:
在横波传播时，当振动传到了第十三个球后，第一个和第十三个球将作完全相同的振动。
当第一个球在平衡位置上并向左运动时（见图70e），第十三个球也在平衡位置，并且也向左运动。
又过了$\frac{1}{4}$周期，第一个球向左运动到最大偏移位置，第十三个球同样也到达这样的位置（见图70f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这两个球的振动相位总是相同的。
**相距最近的振动相位相同的两个点间的距离叫做波长**。
所以，第一个球和第十三个球之间的距离，第二个球和第十四个球之间的距离，第三个球和第十五个球之间的距离都等于波长（见图70e、f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
图71b所示纵波的波长等于第二个球与第十四个球之间的距离，或第四个球与第十六个球之间的距离。
波长用希腊字母$\lambda$表示。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在波传播时，物体的不同点（例如这个模型中的各个球），只要它们之间的距离不等于$n\lambda$（$n$为整数），就以不同的相位振动。
相距$\lambda/2$的第一个球和第七个球（见图70）以相反的相位振动：当第一个球向左运动时，第七个球就向右运动，反过来也是这样。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在一个周期内，波传播的距离为$\lambda$（见图70e）。
因此，波速可由下面的公式求出：
$v=\frac{\lambda}{T}$ (4.1)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
因为周期$T$与频率$\nu$的关系为
$T=\frac{1}{\nu}$，
所以：
$v=\lambda\nu$ (4.2)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: **波速等于波长与振动频率的乘积**。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: 波沿绳传播时，我们可以观察到两种周期性。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text: 39. 波长　波速

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text: 第四章　机械波　声 · 印刷页 100

geometry.fontFamily: ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace

blocks.text:
在横波传播时，当振动传到了第十三个球后，第一个和第十三个球将作完全相同的振动。
当第一个球在平衡位置上并向左运动时（见图70e），第十三个球也在平衡位置，并且也向左运动。
又过了$\frac{1}{4}$周期，第一个球向左运动到最大偏移位置，第十三个球同样也到达这样的位置（见图70f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
这两个球的振动相位总是相同的。
**相距最近的振动相位相同的两个点间的距离叫做波长**。
所以，第一个球和第十三个球之间的距离，第二个球和第十四个球之间的距离，第三个球和第十五个球之间的距离都等于波长（见图70e、f）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif
"Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
图71b所示纵波的波长等于第二个球与第十四个球之间的距离，或第四个球与第十六个球之间的距离。
波长用希腊字母$\lambda$表示。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif
"Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
在波传播时，物体的不同点（例如这个模型中的各个球），只要它们之间的距离不等于$n\lambda$（$n$为整数），就以不同的相位振动。
相距$\lambda/2$的第一个球和第七个球（见图70）以相反的相位振动：当第一个球向左运动时，第七个球就向右运动，反过来也是这样。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
在一个周期内，波传播的距离为$\lambda$（见图70e）。
因此，波速可由下面的公式求出：
$v=\frac{\lambda}{T}$ (4.1)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
因为周期$T$与频率$\nu$的关系为
$T=\frac{1}{\nu}$，
所以：
$v=\lambda\nu$ (4.2)

observed.title: 39. 波长　波速 - 书写题与标准答案

blocks.text: 39. 波长　波速 - 书写题与标准答案

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
1. 什么叫做波？机械波是振动或扰动在弹性介质中的传播。一个质点偏离平衡位置后，通过作用力使相邻质点依次振动，扰动便从一处传到另一处。各质点是在各自的局部位置附近振动，并不是跟着波穿过整个介质。2. 横波与纵波有什么区别？分别举出横波与纵波的例子。横波中，介质质点的振动方向与波的传播方向垂直。例如，把拉紧的绳向侧方拨动，扰动沿绳传播，而各绳段沿垂直于传播方向的方向往复运动。

纵波中，介质质点的振动方向与波的传播方向平行。例如，沿弹簧的长度方向来回推拉一端，密集和稀疏的区域便沿弹簧传播。空气中的声波也是纵波：空气质点沿声音的传播方向来回振动。3. 波动的基本特点是什么？波动的基本特点是：扰动和能量能够沿介质传播，却不伴随介质物质的持续整体输运。在本课的理想机械波模型中，各质点只在自己的平衡位置附近往复振动，并不跟着波一起前进。

例如，在球与弹簧组成的链子中，形变的弹簧对下一个球施力并做功，能量通过弹簧从一个球传向下一个球，而各球仍在各自的局部位置附近振动。这并不是说质点没有运动。4. 什么叫做波长？波长 $\lambda$ 是沿波的传播方向，相距最近的两个不同的同相位振动点之间的距离。同相位的点同时重复相同的振动状态，位移和运动方向都相同。如果两个点只在某一瞬间位移相同，但运动方向相反，就不能据此认为它们同相位。

例如，相邻两个波峰之间的距离，或纵波中相邻两个密集区之间的距离，都是一个波长。图70中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔就是一个波长。5. 波速与波长有什么关系？在一个振动周期 $T$ 内，波形向前传播一个波长 $\lambda$，所以波速为 $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$，其中 $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ 是振动频率。也就是说，波速等于波长与频率的乘积。在频率保持不变时，波长越大，波速越大。这里的波速是波的传播速度，不是某个振动质点的瞬时速度。6. 指出图70中两个相邻的球振动的相位差。图70e中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔等于一个波长，其中有12个相等的相邻间隔，所以相邻间隔为 $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$。

对于已经进入振动的两个相邻球，相位差的大小为 $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ 弧度，即 $30^\circ$。沿波的传播方向，后一个球比前一个球滞后十二分之一周期，相应的时间滞后为 $\frac{T}{12}$。相邻两幅图之间的 $\frac{T}{4}$ 是拍下两幅图的时间间隔，不是相邻两球的振动滞后时间。

exercises.text: 3. 波动的基本特点是什么？

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

details.text:
波动的基本特点是：扰动和能量能够沿介质传播，却不伴随介质物质的持续整体输运。在本课的理想机械波模型中，各质点只在自己的平衡位置附近往复振动，并不跟着波一起前进。

例如，在球与弹簧组成的链子中，形变的弹簧对下一个球施力并做功，能量通过弹簧从一个球传向下一个球，而各球仍在各自的局部位置附近振动。这并不是说质点没有运动。

exercises.text: 4. 什么叫做波长？

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

details.text:
波长 $\lambda$ 是沿波的传播方向，相距最近的两个不同的同相位振动点之间的距离。同相位的点同时重复相同的振动状态，位移和运动方向都相同。如果两个点只在某一瞬间位移相同，但运动方向相反，就不能据此认为它们同相位。

例如，相邻两个波峰之间的距离，或纵波中相邻两个密集区之间的距离，都是一个波长。图70中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔就是一个波长。

exercises.text: 5. 波速与波长有什么关系？

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

details.text: 在一个振动周期 $T$ 内，波形向前传播一个波长 $\lambda$，所以波速为 $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$，其中 $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ 是振动频率。也就是说，波速等于波长与频率的乘积。在频率保持不变时，波长越大，波速越大。这里的波速是波的传播速度，不是某个振动质点的瞬时速度。

exercises.text: 6. 指出图70中两个相邻的球振动的相位差。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

details.text:
图70e中，第1球到第13球沿未扰动链线的间隔等于一个波长，其中有12个相等的相邻间隔，所以相邻间隔为 $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$。

对于已经进入振动的两个相邻球，相位差的大小为 $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ 弧度，即 $30^\circ$。沿波的传播方向，后一个球比前一个球滞后十二分之一周期，相应的时间滞后为 $\frac{T}{12}$。相邻两幅图之间的 $\frac{T}{4}$ 是拍下两幅图的时间间隔，不是相邻两球的振动滞后时间。

observed.title: 39. Wavelength and Wave Speed

paragraphs.text:
Once the transverse wave reaches the thirteenth ball, it and the first ball vibrate identically.
Both pass equilibrium moving left together (Figure 70e).

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
After another $\frac{1}{4}$ of a period, both reach their maximum leftward displacement (Figure 70f).
Their phase is always the same.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**Wavelength is the distance between nearest in-phase points**.
The first and thirteenth, second and fourteenth, and third and fifteenth balls share this spacing (Figure 70e, f).

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
For the longitudinal wave in Figure 71b, a wavelength separates the second and fourteenth balls or the fourth and sixteenth.
Wavelength is denoted by the Greek letter $\lambda$.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Phase differs except across $n\lambda$ (integer $n$).
Balls one and seven, $\lambda/2$ apart, are in antiphase: one moves left as the other moves right, and vice versa (Figure 70).

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
In one period, a wave travels a distance $\lambda$ (see Figure 70e).
Its speed is therefore given by
$v=\frac{\lambda}{T}$ (4.1)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Since the period $T$ and frequency $\nu$ are related by
$T=\frac{1}{\nu}$,
it follows that:
$v=\lambda\nu$ (4.2)

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: **Wave speed equals wavelength multiplied by the vibration frequency**.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: When a wave travels along a string, we can observe two kinds of periodicity.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Each point on the string repeats its motion periodically.
For harmonic sine or cosine motion, all points have the same frequency and amplitude, but differ in phase.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
At any instant, the profile repeats at intervals of $\lambda$.
Figure 72 shows this profile as the curve through $O$.
The whole shape moves rightward at speed $v$ as time passes.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
After a time interval
$\Delta t=\frac{\Delta s}{v}$
the wave has the shape shown by the curve that does not pass through $O$.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: Equation (4.2), which relates wave speed, wavelength, and vibration frequency, also applies to longitudinal waves.

When a wave travels along a string, we can observe two kinds of periodicity.

Each point on the string repeats its motion periodically.
For harmonic sine or cosine motion, all points have the same frequency and amplitude, but differ in phase.

At any instant, the profile repeats at intervals of $\lambda$.
Figure 72 shows this profile as the curve through $O$.
The whole shape moves rightward at speed $v$ as time passes.
Figure 72

After a time interval
$\Delta t=\frac{\Delta s}{v}$
the wave has the shape shown by the curve that does not pass through $O$.
Equation (4.2), which relates wave speed, wavelength, and vibration frequency, also applies to longitudinal waves.

blocks.text: 39. Wavelength and Wave Speed - Written Questions and Standard Answers

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
1. What is a wave?A mechanical wave is an oscillation or disturbance that propagates through an elastic medium. A displaced particle exerts forces on its neighbors, making them oscillate in turn, so the disturbance spreads from place to place. The particles vibrate locally; they do not travel through the medium with the wave.2. How do transverse and longitudinal waves differ? Give examples of each.In a transverse wave, the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction in which the wave travels. For example, a sideways disturbance travels along a stretched cord while each part of the cord moves across that direction.

In a longitudinal wave, the particles vibrate parallel to the direction in which the wave travels. Pushing and pulling a spring along its length produces traveling compressions and rarefactions. Sound in air is also longitudinal: air particles oscillate back and forth along the direction of sound propagation.3. What is the basic characteristic of wave motion?The basic characteristic of wave motion is that the disturbance and energy travel through the medium without sustained bulk transport of its mass. In the ideal mechanical-wave model, each particle oscillates about its own equilibrium position rather than moving along with the wave.

For example, in the ball-and-spring chain, a deformed spring exerts a force and does work on the next ball. Energy passes from ball to ball through the springs, while the balls remain local oscillators. This does not mean that the particles are motionless.4. What is wavelength?Wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance along the direction of propagation between the nearest distinct points vibrating in the same phase. Such points repeat the same vibration state together, with the same displacement and direction of motion. Equal displacement at just one instant is not sufficient if their directions of motion differ.

Examples are the distance from one crest to the next crest, or from one compression to the next compression. In Figure 70, the separation along the undisturbed chain from ball 1 to ball 13 is one wavelength.5. How are wave speed and wavelength related?In one vibration period $T$, the wave pattern travels one wavelength $\lambda$. Therefore its propagation speed is $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$, where $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ is the vibration frequency. Wave speed equals wavelength multiplied by frequency. At a fixed frequency, a larger wavelength corresponds to a larger wave speed. This is the wave's propagation speed, not the instantaneous velocity of a vibrating particle.6. State the phase difference between the vibrations of two adjacent balls in Figure 70.In Figure 70e, one wavelength extends from ball 1 to ball 13, covering twelve equal adjacent intervals along the undisturbed chain. The adjacent spacing is therefore $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$.

For two adjacent balls that have entered the vibration, the phase-difference magnitude is $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians, or $30^\circ$. Along the direction of propagation, the next ball lags the preceding ball by one twelfth of a cycle, corresponding to a time delay $\frac{T}{12}$. The $\frac{T}{4}$ interval between successive panels is not the delay between adjacent balls.

details.text:
In Figure 70e, one wavelength extends from ball 1 to ball 13, covering twelve equal adjacent intervals along the undisturbed chain. The adjacent spacing is therefore $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$.

For two adjacent balls that have entered the vibration, the phase-difference magnitude is $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians, or $30^\circ$. Along the direction of propagation, the next ball lags the preceding ball by one twelfth of a cycle, corresponding to a time delay $\frac{T}{12}$. The $\frac{T}{4}$ interval between successive panels is not the delay between adjacent balls.

expectedVisibleFragments: 1. What is a wave?

A mechanical wave is an oscillation or disturbance that propagates through an elastic medium. A displaced particle exerts forces on its neighbors, making them oscillate in turn, so the disturbance spreads from place to place. The particles vibrate locally; they do not travel through the medium with the wave.
2. How do transverse and longitudinal waves differ? Give examples of each.

In a transverse wave, the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction in which the wave travels. For example, a sideways disturbance travels along a stretched cord while each part of the cord moves across that direction.

In a longitudinal wave, the particles vibrate parallel to the direction in which the wave travels. Pushing and pulling a spring along its length produces traveling compressions and rarefactions. Sound in air is also longitudinal: air particles oscillate back and forth along the direction of sound propagation.
3. What is the basic characteristic of wave motion?

The basic characteristic of wave motion is that the disturbance and energy travel through the medium without sustained bulk transport of its mass. In the ideal mechanical-wave model, each particle oscillates about its own equilibrium position rather than moving along with the wave.

For example, in the ball-and-spring chain, a deformed spring exerts a force and does work on the next ball. Energy passes from ball to ball through the springs, while the balls remain local oscillators. This does not mean that the particles are motionless.
4. What is wavelength?

Wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance along the direction of propagation between the nearest distinct points vibrating in the same phase. Such points repeat the same vibration state together, with the same displacement and direction of motion. Equal displacement at just one instant is not sufficient if their directions of motion differ.

Examples are the distance from one crest to the next crest, or from one compression to the next compression. In Figure 70, the separation along the undisturbed chain from ball 1 to ball 13 is one wavelength.
5. How are wave speed and wavelength related?

In one vibration period $T$, the wave pattern travels one wavelength $\lambda$. Therefore its propagation speed is $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$, where $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ is the vibration frequency. Wave speed equals wavelength multiplied by frequency. At a fixed frequency, a larger wavelength corresponds to a larger wave speed. This is the wave's propagation speed, not the instantaneous velocity of a vibrating particle.
6. State the phase difference between the vibrations of two adjacent balls in Figure 70.

In Figure 70e, one wavelength extends from ball 1 to ball 13, covering twelve equal adjacent intervals along the undisturbed chain. The adjacent spacing is therefore $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$.

For two adjacent balls that have entered the vibration, the phase-difference magnitude is $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians, or $30^\circ$. Along the direction of propagation, the next ball lags the preceding ball by one twelfth of a cycle, corresponding to a time delay $\frac{T}{12}$. The $\frac{T}{4}$ interval between successive panels is not the delay between adjacent balls.

texts:
Once the transverse wave reaches the thirteenth ball, it and the first ball vibrate identically.
Both pass equilibrium moving left together (Figure 70e).

After another $\frac{1}{4}$ of a period, both reach their maximum leftward displacement (Figure 70f).
Their phase is always the same.

**Wavelength is the distance between nearest in-phase points**.
The first and thirteenth, second and fourteenth, and third and fifteenth balls share this spacing (Figure 70e, f).

For the longitudinal wave in Figure 71b, a wavelength separates the second and fourteenth balls or the fourth and sixteenth.
Wavelength is denoted by the Greek letter $\lambda$.

Phase differs except across $n\lambda$ (integer $n$).
Balls one and seven, $\lambda/2$ apart, are in antiphase: one moves left as the other moves right, and vice versa (Figure 70).

In one period, a wave travels a distance $\lambda$ (see Figure 70e).
Its speed is therefore given by
$v=\frac{\lambda}{T}$ (4.1)

Since the period $T$ and frequency $\nu$ are related by
$T=\frac{1}{\nu}$,
it follows that:
$v=\lambda\nu$ (4.2)
**Wave speed equals wavelength multiplied by the vibration frequency**.
When a wave travels along a string, we can observe two kinds of periodicity.

Each point on the string repeats its motion periodically.
For harmonic sine or cosine motion, all points have the same frequency and amplitude, but differ in phase.

At any instant, the profile repeats at intervals of $\lambda$.
Figure 72 shows this profile as the curve through $O$.
The whole shape moves rightward at speed $v$ as time passes.
Figure 72

After a time interval
$\Delta t=\frac{\Delta s}{v}$
the wave has the shape shown by the curve that does not pass through $O$.
Equation (4.2), which relates wave speed, wavelength, and vibration frequency, also applies to longitudinal waves.

observed.title: 39. Wavelength and Wave Speed - Written Questions and Standard Answers

blocks.text: 39. Wavelength and Wave Speed - Written Questions and Standard Answers

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text:
1. What is a wave?A mechanical wave is an oscillation or disturbance that propagates through an elastic medium. A displaced particle exerts forces on its neighbors, making them oscillate in turn, so the disturbance spreads from place to place. The particles vibrate locally; they do not travel through the medium with the wave.2. How do transverse and longitudinal waves differ? Give examples of each.In a transverse wave, the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction in which the wave travels. For example, a sideways disturbance travels along a stretched cord while each part of the cord moves across that direction.

In a longitudinal wave, the particles vibrate parallel to the direction in which the wave travels. Pushing and pulling a spring along its length produces traveling compressions and rarefactions. Sound in air is also longitudinal: air particles oscillate back and forth along the direction of sound propagation.3. What is the basic characteristic of wave motion?The basic characteristic of wave motion is that the disturbance and energy travel through the medium without sustained bulk transport of its mass. In the ideal mechanical-wave model, each particle oscillates about its own equilibrium position rather than moving along with the wave.

For example, in the ball-and-spring chain, a deformed spring exerts a force and does work on the next ball. Energy passes from ball to ball through the springs, while the balls remain local oscillators. This does not mean that the particles are motionless.4. What is wavelength?Wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance along the direction of propagation between the nearest distinct points vibrating in the same phase. Such points repeat the same vibration state together, with the same displacement and direction of motion. Equal displacement at just one instant is not sufficient if their directions of motion differ.

Examples are the distance from one crest to the next crest, or from one compression to the next compression. In Figure 70, the separation along the undisturbed chain from ball 1 to ball 13 is one wavelength.5. How are wave speed and wavelength related?In one vibration period $T$, the wave pattern travels one wavelength $\lambda$. Therefore its propagation speed is $v=\frac{\lambda}{T}=\lambda\nu$, where $\nu=\frac{1}{T}$ is the vibration frequency. Wave speed equals wavelength multiplied by frequency. At a fixed frequency, a larger wavelength corresponds to a larger wave speed. This is the wave's propagation speed, not the instantaneous velocity of a vibrating particle.6. State the phase difference between the vibrations of two adjacent balls in Figure 70.In Figure 70e, one wavelength extends from ball 1 to ball 13, covering twelve equal adjacent intervals along the undisturbed chain. The adjacent spacing is therefore $d=\frac{\lambda}{12}$.

For two adjacent balls that have entered the vibration, the phase-difference magnitude is $|\Delta\phi|=\frac{2\pi d}{\lambda}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians, or $30^\circ$. Along the direction of propagation, the next ball lags the preceding ball by one twelfth of a cycle, corresponding to a time delay $\frac{T}{12}$. The $\frac{T}{4}$ interval between successive panels is not the delay between adjacent balls.

A displaced particle exerts forces on its neighbors, making them oscillate in turn, so the disturbance spreads from place to place. The basic characteristic of wave motion is that the disturbance and energy travel through the medium without sustained bulk transport of its mass. In the ideal mechanical-wave model, each particle oscillates about its own equilibrium position rather than moving along with the wave.

observed.title: 40. 媒质中的波

paragraphs.text:
对于细长的橡皮绳、弦或杆，可以把波沿其长度方向的传播近似看作一维传播。
波可以沿这条轴线向任一侧传播，并不只限于某一个朝向。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
气体、液体或固体连续地充满一片空间时，可以把它看作连续介质。
局部扰动能通过介质各部分之间的相互作用，向多个方向传播。
实际的传播方向和形态取决于波源与介质，局部振动依次传递的基本过程仍与前面相同。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波在一片空间中传播，还会表现出一些新的特点。
下面从能量的扩散和波面的形状来认识这些特点。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波从局部波源向外传播时，可以扩展到越来越大的区域。
图64中的石头落水所激起的环形波，直观地展示了这种扩展。
这是水面上的波，并不是水体内部的球面波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波源送出的能量随波的传播，分布到越来越宽广的波面上。
一秒钟内通过单位面积的能量，可以用来描述能量通量的大小。
在稳定、均匀向外扩散且没有额外能量输入的情况下，离波源越远，这一通量越小。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
对于同一介质、相同频率等条件下的小振幅振动，能量与振幅的平方成正比，因此通量减小时振幅也会减小。
这一关系与第11节讨论的振动能量关系相同。
它适用于相应的小振动模型，包括弹簧重物、摆锤以及介质局部质点的振动，并不是任意大幅振动都满足的定律。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
几何扩散本身就能使振幅随距离减小，即使介质没有耗散也会如此。
这种减小不需要机械能因摩擦等作用而转化成内能，不能与吸收造成的衰减混为一谈。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**理想平面波**没有上述几何扩散。
让大片薄板沿其法线方向振动，可以在适当条件下近似产生平面波。
这里假定介质均匀、各向同性，并且薄板各处受到一致的驱动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
与板接触的介质质点便以相同振幅和相同相位振动，扰动沿板的法线方向传播。
位于每一个平行于薄板的平面上的质点，具有相同相位。
**等相位的面叫做波面，平面波的波面是平面**（图73）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
真实薄板的大小有限，远离边缘的区域才可能近似符合这个模型。
在边缘附近，衍射会使波面弯曲，实际波并不是处处都保持理想平面波的形态。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**垂直于波面的线叫做波射线**，平面波的波射线是相互平行的直线。
在这里采用的均匀、各向同性介质模型中，波射线表示波的传播方向。
在这种射线描述下，波的能量也沿波射线传播，不能把这一方向关系无条件推广到所有复杂介质。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
理想平面波传播时，垂直于传播方向的横截面积不随距离增大，能量没有几何扩散。
在均匀、无耗散的介质中，它的振幅保持不变。
耗散能使振幅减小，而实际有限宽度的波束还可能在边缘扩散，因此不能把所有振幅减小都归因于摩擦。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
水面上的**线波**能为认识空间中的平面波提供直观类比。
让一根杆轻轻接触水面，并使杆上下振动，就能在适当条件下形成近似直线的波面。
远离杆的两端时，位于平行于杆的直线上的水面质点近似同相位振动（图74）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: 这仍是液面波的波面，不能把这种类比当成液体内部传播平面剪切波的证据。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
连续介质中的另一种例子是**球面波**，也叫球形波。
在均匀、各向同性的介质中，一个均匀脉动的球面可以向外产生球面波（图75）。
波面是以波源中心为球心的球面，波射线沿半径的延长线向外。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在稳定、均匀向外传播且无吸收的球面波模型中，通过各个包围波源的球面的总功率相同。
球面的半径越大，面积就越大，能量便分布在更大的面积上，单位面积的能量通量随之减小。
在介质性质、频率等条件相同时，振幅也随半径增大而减小，这是几何扩散，不要求有能量吸收。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在**横波**中，质点的位移方向垂直于波的传播方向。
固体内部的弹性横波涉及**切变**，也叫剪切形变，物质各层彼此相对错动。
在小形变的纯剪切模型中，体积在一阶近似下不变。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
有剪切刚度的弹性固体发生这种形变时，会产生使它恢复原状的弹力。
这些恢复力使介质的各部分发生局部振动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这里讨论的普通液体和气体没有静态剪切刚度，各层相对错动时没有固体那样的剪切恢复力。
因此，在这一普通流体模型中，液体和气体内部不能传播弹性剪切横波。
有剪切刚度的固体可以传播这类横波，液体表面的情况则要按脚注①另作区分。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
① 液体表面的波可以包含上下的横向位移，质点运动也可能同时包含水平分量，并不一定是纯横波。
液面的恢复作用来自重力和表面张力，这不意味着普通液体内部具有传播弹性剪切横波所需的剪切刚度。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**纵波**的质点位移方向沿波的传播方向，在固体中表现为压缩与拉伸形变（见第37节）。
在普通液体和气体中，它表现为压缩与稀疏，并不要求流体维持拉伸应力。
固体、液体和气体在体积受到压缩时都有相应的恢复作用，因此都能传播纵波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在通常采用的各向同性弹性岩石模型中，纵向的P波比横向的S波传播得快。
因此，地震观测站通常先记录到P波，随后记录到同一次地震产生的S波。
两种波到达的时间差，可以用来估算震源到观测站的距离。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这种估算需要合适的P波、S波传播速度及路径模型，实际地壳并不是处处均匀的。
单个观测站的时间差可以提供距离信息，但不能独自唯一确定震源的位置。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text: 40. 媒质中的波

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

blocks.text: 第四章　机械波　声 · 印刷页 102

远离杆的两端时，位于平行于杆的直线上的水面质点近似同相位振动（图74）。这仍是液面波的波面，不能把这种类比当成液体内部传播平面剪切波的证据。图74图75连续介质中的另一种例子是**球面波**，也叫球形波。
在均匀、各向同性的介质中，一个均匀脉动的球面可以向外产生球面波（图75）。
波面是以波源中心为球心的球面，波射线沿半径的延长线向外。在稳定、均匀向外传播且无吸收的球面波模型中，通过各个包围波源的球面的总功率相同。
球面的半径越大，面积就越大，能量便分布在更大的面积上，单位面积的能量通量随之减小。
在介质性质、频率等条件相同时，振幅也随半径增大而减小，这是几何扩散，不要求有能量吸收。在**横波**中，质点的位移方向垂直于波的传播方向。
固体内部的弹性横波涉及**切变**，也叫剪切形变，物质各层彼此相对错动。
在小形变的纯剪切模型中，体积在一阶近似下不变。有剪切刚度的弹性固体发生这种形变时，会产生使它恢复原状的弹力。
这些恢复力使介质的各部分发生局部振动。这里讨论的普通液体和气体没有静态剪切刚度，各层相对错动时没有固体那样的剪切恢复力。

有剪切刚度的固体可以传播这类横波，液体表面的情况则要按脚注①另作区分。① 液体表面的波可以包含上下的横向位移，质点运动也可能同时包含水平分量，并不一定是纯横波。
液面的恢复作用来自重力和表面张力，这不意味着普通液体内部具有传播弹性剪切横波所需的剪切刚度。**纵波**的质点位移方向沿波的传播方向，在固体中表现为压缩与拉伸形变（见第37节）。
在普通液体和气体中，它表现为压缩与稀疏，并不要求流体维持拉伸应力。
固体、液体和气体在体积受到压缩时都有相应的恢复作用，因此都能传播纵波。在通常采用的各向同性弹性岩石模型中，纵向的P波比横向的S波传播得快。
因此，地震观测站通常先记录到P波，随后记录到同一次地震产生的S波。
两种波到达的时间差，可以用来估算震源到观测站的距离。这种估算需要合适的P波、S波传播速度及路径模型，实际地壳并不是处处均匀的。
单个观测站的时间差可以提供距离信息，但不能独自唯一确定震源的位置。

波可以沿这条轴线向任一侧传播，并不只限于某一个朝向。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
气体、液体或固体连续地充满一片空间时，可以把它看作连续介质。
局部扰动能通过介质各部分之间的相互作用，向多个方向传播。
实际的传播方向和形态取决于波源与介质，局部振动依次传递的基本过程仍与前面相同。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波在一片空间中传播，还会表现出一些新的特点。
下面从能量的扩散和波面的形状来认识这些特点。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波从局部波源向外传播时，可以扩展到越来越大的区域。
图64中的石头落水所激起的环形波，直观地展示了这种扩展。
这是水面上的波，并不是水体内部的球面波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
波源送出的能量随波的传播，分布到越来越宽广的波面上。
一秒钟内通过单位面积的能量，可以用来描述能量通量的大小。
在稳定、均匀向外扩散且没有额外能量输入的情况下，离波源越远，这一通量越小。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
对于同一介质、相同频率等条件下的小振幅振动，能量与振幅的平方成正比，因此通量减小时振幅也会减小。
这一关系与第11节讨论的振动能量关系相同。
它适用于相应的小振动模型，包括弹簧重物、摆锤以及介质局部质点的振动，并不是任意大幅振动都满足的定律。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
几何扩散本身就能使振幅随距离减小，即使介质没有耗散也会如此。
这种减小不需要机械能因摩擦等作用而转化成内能，不能与吸收造成的衰减混为一谈。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**理想平面波**没有上述几何扩散。
让大片薄板沿其法线方向振动，可以在适当条件下近似产生平面波。
这里假定介质均匀、各向同性，并且薄板各处受到一致的驱动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
与板接触的介质质点便以相同振幅和相同相位振动，扰动沿板的法线方向传播。
位于每一个平行于薄板的平面上的质点，具有相同相位。
**等相位的面叫做波面，平面波的波面是平面**（图73）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
真实薄板的大小有限，远离边缘的区域才可能近似符合这个模型。
在边缘附近，衍射会使波面弯曲，实际波并不是处处都保持理想平面波的形态。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**垂直于波面的线叫做波射线**，平面波的波射线是相互平行的直线。
在这里采用的均匀、各向同性介质模型中，波射线表示波的传播方向。
在这种射线描述下，波的能量也沿波射线传播，不能把这一方向关系无条件推广到所有复杂介质。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
理想平面波传播时，垂直于传播方向的横截面积不随距离增大，能量没有几何扩散。
在均匀、无耗散的介质中，它的振幅保持不变。
耗散能使振幅减小，而实际有限宽度的波束还可能在边缘扩散，因此不能把所有振幅减小都归因于摩擦。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
水面上的**线波**能为认识空间中的平面波提供直观类比。
让一根杆轻轻接触水面，并使杆上下振动，就能在适当条件下形成近似直线的波面。
远离杆的两端时，位于平行于杆的直线上的水面质点近似同相位振动（图74）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: 这仍是液面波的波面，不能把这种类比当成液体内部传播平面剪切波的证据。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
连续介质中的另一种例子是**球面波**，也叫球形波。
在均匀、各向同性的介质中，一个均匀脉动的球面可以向外产生球面波（图75）。
波面是以波源中心为球心的球面，波射线沿半径的延长线向外。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在稳定、均匀向外传播且无吸收的球面波模型中，通过各个包围波源的球面的总功率相同。
球面的半径越大，面积就越大，能量便分布在更大的面积上，单位面积的能量通量随之减小。
在介质性质、频率等条件相同时，振幅也随半径增大而减小，这是几何扩散，不要求有能量吸收。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在**横波**中，质点的位移方向垂直于波的传播方向。
固体内部的弹性横波涉及**切变**，也叫剪切形变，物质各层彼此相对错动。
在小形变的纯剪切模型中，体积在一阶近似下不变。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
有剪切刚度的弹性固体发生这种形变时，会产生使它恢复原状的弹力。
这些恢复力使介质的各部分发生局部振动。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这里讨论的普通液体和气体没有静态剪切刚度，各层相对错动时没有固体那样的剪切恢复力。
因此，在这一普通流体模型中，液体和气体内部不能传播弹性剪切横波。
有剪切刚度的固体可以传播这类横波，液体表面的情况则要按脚注①另作区分。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
① 液体表面的波可以包含上下的横向位移，质点运动也可能同时包含水平分量，并不一定是纯横波。
液面的恢复作用来自重力和表面张力，这不意味着普通液体内部具有传播弹性剪切横波所需的剪切刚度。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
**纵波**的质点位移方向沿波的传播方向，在固体中表现为压缩与拉伸形变（见第37节）。
在普通液体和气体中，它表现为压缩与稀疏，并不要求流体维持拉伸应力。
固体、液体和气体在体积受到压缩时都有相应的恢复作用，因此都能传播纵波。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在通常采用的各向同性弹性岩石模型中，纵向的P波比横向的S波传播得快。
因此，地震观测站通常先记录到P波，随后记录到同一次地震产生的S波。
两种波到达的时间差，可以用来估算震源到观测站的距离。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
这种估算需要合适的P波、S波传播速度及路径模型，实际地壳并不是处处均匀的。
单个观测站的时间差可以提供距离信息，但不能独自唯一确定震源的位置。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

在稳定、均匀向外扩散且没有额外能量输入的情况下，离波源越远，这一通量越小。对于同一介质、相同频率等条件下的小振幅振动，能量与振幅的平方成正比，因此通量减小时振幅也会减小。
这一关系与第11节讨论的振动能量关系相同。
它适用于相应的小振动模型，包括弹簧重物、摆锤以及介质局部质点的振动，并不是任意大幅振动都满足的定律。几何扩散本身就能使振幅随距离减小，即使介质没有耗散也会如此。
这种减小不需要机械能因摩擦等作用而转化成内能，不能与吸收造成的衰减混为一谈。**理想平面波**没有上述几何扩散。
让大片薄板沿其法线方向振动，可以在适当条件下近似产生平面波。
这里假定介质均匀、各向同性，并且薄板各处受到一致的驱动。与板接触的介质质点便以相同振幅和相同相位振动，扰动沿板的法线方向传播。
位于每一个平行于薄板的平面上的质点，具有相同相位。
**等相位的面叫做波面，平面波的波面是平面**（图73）。真实薄板的大小有限，远离边缘的区域才可能近似符合这个模型。
在边缘附近，衍射会使波面弯曲，实际波并不是处处都保持理想平面波的形态。图73**垂直于波面的线叫做波射线**，平面波的波射线是相互平行的直线。
在这里采用的均匀、各向同性介质模型中，波射线表示波的传播方向。
在这种射线描述下，波的能量也沿波射线传播，不能把这一方向关系无条件推广到所有复杂介质。理想平面波传播时，垂直于传播方向的横截面积不随距离增大，能量没有几何扩散。
在均匀、无耗散的介质中，它的振幅保持不变。
耗散能使振幅减小，而实际有限宽度的波束还可能在边缘扩散，因此不能把所有振幅减小都归因于摩擦。水面上的**线波**能为认识空间中的平面波提供直观类比。
让一根杆轻轻接触水面，并使杆上下振动，就能在适当条件下形成近似直线的波面。
远离杆的两端时，位于平行于杆的直线上的水面质点近似同相位振动（图74）。这仍是液面波的波面，不能把这种类比当成液体内部传播平面剪切波的证据。图74图75连续介质中的另一种例子是**球面波**，也叫球形波。
在均匀、各向同性的介质中，一个均匀脉动的球面可以向外产生球面波（图75）。
波面是以波源中心为球心的球面，波射线沿半径的延长线向外。在稳定、均匀向外传播且无吸收的球面波模型中，通过各个包围波源的球面的总功率相同。
球面的半径越大，面积就越大，能量便分布在更大的面积上，单位面积的能量通量随之减小。
在介质性质、频率等条件相同时，振幅也随半径增大而减小，这是几何扩散，不要求有能量吸收。在**横波**中，质点的位移方向垂直于波的传播方向。
固体内部的弹性横波涉及**切变**，也叫剪切形变，物质各层彼此相对错动。
在小形变的纯剪切模型中，体积在一阶近似下不变。有剪切刚度的弹性固体发生这种形变时，会产生使它恢复原状的弹力。
这些恢复力使介质的各部分发生局部振动。这里讨论的普通液体和气体没有静态剪切刚度，各层相对错动时没有固体那样的剪切恢复力。
因此，在这一普通流体模型中，液体和气体内部不能传播弹性剪切横波。
有剪切刚度的固体可以传播这类横波，液体表面的情况则要按脚注①另作区分。① 液体表面的波可以包含上下的横向位移，质点运动也可能同时包含水平分量，并不一定是纯横波。
液面的恢复作用来自重力和表面张力，这不意味着普通液体内部具有传播弹性剪切横波所需的剪切刚度。**纵波**的质点位移方向沿波的传播方向，在固体中表现为压缩与拉伸形变（见第37节）。
在普通液体和气体中，它表现为压缩与稀疏，并不要求流体维持拉伸应力。
固体、液体和气体在体积受到压缩时都有相应的恢复作用，因此都能传播纵波。在通常采用的各向同性弹性岩石模型中，纵向的P波比横向的S波传播得快。
因此，地震观测站通常先记录到P波，随后记录到同一次地震产生的S波。
两种波到达的时间差，可以用来估算震源到观测站的距离。这种估算需要合适的P波、S波传播速度及路径模型，实际地壳并不是处处均匀的。
单个观测站的时间差可以提供距离信息，但不能独自唯一确定震源的位置。

paragraphs.text:

paragraphs.text:

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:

For steady, uniform spreading with no added energy, this flux falls with distance.

paragraphs.text:

paragraphs.text:

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:

Points touching the plate then oscillate with equal amplitude and phase.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Points on each plane parallel to the plate have the same phase.
An equal-phase surface is called a **wavefront**.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:

paragraphs.text:

For a plane wave, these normals form parallel straight lines.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:

In this ray description, wave energy travels along the rays.

paragraphs.text:

In a uniform lossless medium, its amplitude therefore stays constant.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: Dissipation can reduce it, while real finite beams may also spread at their edges.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Straight water-surface waves provide a visible analogy to plane waves.
To produce them, let a rod lightly touch the water and move it up and down.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Away from the rod ends, points on lines parallel to it have nearly equal phase (Figure 74).

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
A uniformly pulsating sphere can produce **spherical waves** (Figure 75).
In a uniform, isotropic medium, the outgoing wavefronts are spherical.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
They are spheres centered on the source.
The rays point outward along the extensions of the radii.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: For steady, uniform spherical spreading without absorption, each sphere carries the same power.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Larger spheres have more area, so less energy crosses each unit of area in one second.
With the medium and frequency fixed, the amplitude decreases with radius.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text: This is geometric spreading, which occurs even without absorption.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
In a **transverse wave**, particle displacement is perpendicular to propagation.
A transverse bulk wave in a solid involves **shear deformation**.
Layers shift past one another.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
In the small, pure-shear model, there is no volume change to first order.
In an elastic solid, shear produces restoring forces.
These forces drive the local oscillations.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Here, ordinary liquids and gases have no static shear stiffness.
They cannot carry bulk elastic shear waves in this model.
Solids can carry them, with the surface qualification in ①.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
① Liquid-surface waves can move particles both vertically and horizontally.
Gravity and surface tension restore the surface, not bulk shear elasticity.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
A **longitudinal wave** has displacement along propagation (Section 37).
In a solid, it involves compression and extension.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
In an ordinary liquid or gas, it involves compression and rarefaction.
This does not require the fluid to sustain tensile stress.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Bulk compression produces restoring effects in all these media.
Solids, liquids, and gases can therefore carry longitudinal waves.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
In the usual isotropic elastic model of rock, longitudinal P waves travel faster than transverse S waves.
A station therefore normally records P waves first.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
S waves from the same earthquake arrive later.
Their arrival-time difference helps estimate the distance to the source.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
The estimate requires suitable P- and S-wave speeds and a model of their paths.
One station's delay alone does not uniquely locate the source.

Along a slender cord, string, or rod, a wave travels mainly along its length.
It can travel either way along this axis.

A gas, liquid, or solid can form a continuous medium.
A local disturbance can spread in many directions within it.
The source and medium set the pattern through local interactions.

Propagation through a region adds some new features.
We now examine spreading and the shape of wavefronts.

An outward-moving wave can spread over a growing region.
The circular water ripples in Figure 64 illustrate this spreading.

They are surface waves, not spherical waves inside the water.
The energy from the source is shared over a widening front.

Energy crossing unit area in one second measures energy flux.
For steady, uniform spreading with no added energy, this flux falls with distance.

With other conditions fixed, small-oscillation energy scales with amplitude squared.
This is the relation discussed in Section 11, so a falling flux means a smaller amplitude.
It applies to small oscillations of a spring mass, a pendulum, and local medium particles.

Geometric spreading can reduce amplitude even in a lossless medium.
This decrease needs no conversion of mechanical energy into internal energy.

An **ideal plane wave** does not undergo geometric spreading.
A large thin plate oscillating perpendicular to its surface can approximate such a wave.

Assume a uniform, isotropic elastic medium and uniform driving.
Points touching the plate then oscillate with equal amplitude and phase.
The wave travels normal to the plate.

Points on each plane parallel to the plate have the same phase.
An equal-phase surface is called a **wavefront**.
Plane-wave wavefronts are planes (Figure 73).

A finite plate gives only an approximation away from its edges.
Near an edge, diffraction bends the wavefronts.
Figure 73

**A wave ray is a line normal to a wavefront.**
For a plane wave, these normals form parallel straight lines.

In a uniform, isotropic medium, rays also show the propagation direction.
In this ray description, wave energy travels along the rays.

An ideal plane wave keeps a fixed cross-sectional area as it travels.
In a uniform lossless medium, its amplitude therefore stays constant.
Dissipation can reduce it, while real finite beams may also spread at their edges.

Straight water-surface waves provide a visible analogy to plane waves.
To produce them, let a rod lightly touch the water and move it up and down.

Away from the rod ends, points on lines parallel to it have nearly equal phase (Figure 74).
These are surface wavefronts, not plane shear waves in the liquid bulk.
Figure 74
Figure 75

A uniformly pulsating sphere can produce **spherical waves** (Figure 75).
In a uniform, isotropic medium, the outgoing wavefronts are spherical.

They are spheres centered on the source.
The rays point outward along the extensions of the radii.
For steady, uniform spherical spreading without absorption, each sphere carries the same power.

Larger spheres have more area, so less energy crosses each unit of area in one second.
With the medium and frequency fixed, the amplitude decreases with radius.
This is geometric spreading, which occurs even without absorption.

In a **transverse wave**, particle displacement is perpendicular to propagation.
A transverse bulk wave in a solid involves **shear deformation**.
Layers shift past one another.

In the small, pure-shear model, there is no volume change to first order.
In an elastic solid, shear produces restoring forces.
These forces drive the local oscillations.

Here, ordinary liquids and gases have no static shear stiffness.
They cannot carry bulk elastic shear waves in this model.
Solids can carry them, with the surface qualification in ①.

① Liquid-surface waves can move particles both vertically and horizontally.
Gravity and surface tension restore the surface, not bulk shear elasticity.

A **longitudinal wave** has displacement along propagation (Section 37).
In a solid, it involves compression and extension.

In an ordinary liquid or gas, it involves compression and rarefaction.
This does not require the fluid to sustain tensile stress.

Bulk compression produces restoring effects in all these media.
Solids, liquids, and gases can therefore carry longitudinal waves.

In the usual isotropic elastic model of rock, longitudinal P waves travel faster than transverse S waves.
A station therefore normally records P waves first.

These are surface wavefronts, not plane shear waves in the liquid bulk.
Figure 74
Figure 75

A uniformly pulsating sphere can produce **spherical waves** (Figure 75).
In a uniform, isotropic medium, the outgoing wavefronts are spherical.

They are spheres centered on the source.
The rays point outward along the extensions of the radii.
For steady, uniform spherical spreading without absorption, each sphere carries the same power.

Larger spheres have more area, so less energy crosses each unit of area in one second.
With the medium and frequency fixed, the amplitude decreases with radius.
This is geometric spreading, which occurs even without absorption.

In a **transverse wave**, particle displacement is perpendicular to propagation.
A transverse bulk wave in a solid involves **shear deformation**.
Layers shift past one another.

In the small, pure-shear model, there is no volume change to first order.
In an elastic solid, shear produces restoring forces.
These forces drive the local oscillations.

Here, ordinary liquids and gases have no static shear stiffness.
They cannot carry bulk elastic shear waves in this model.
Solids can carry them, with the surface qualification in ①.

① Liquid-surface waves can move particles both vertically and horizontally.
Gravity and surface tension restore the surface, not bulk shear elasticity.

A **longitudinal wave** has displacement along propagation (Section 37).
In a solid, it involves compression and extension.

In an ordinary liquid or gas, it involves compression and rarefaction.
This does not require the fluid to sustain tensile stress.

Bulk compression produces restoring effects in all these media.
Solids, liquids, and gases can therefore carry longitudinal waves.

In the usual isotropic elastic model of rock, longitudinal P waves travel faster than transverse S waves.
A station therefore normally records P waves first.

S waves from the same earthquake arrive later.
Their arrival-time difference helps estimate the distance to the source.

The estimate requires suitable P- and S-wave speeds and a model of their paths.
One station's delay alone does not uniquely locate the source.

observed.title: 44. 声的共鸣

paragraphs.text:
发声物体可以做自由振动。
在周期性外力作用下，它也可以做受迫振动。
外力频率接近物体的固有频率时，受迫振动可以显著增强，这就是共振。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
两只相同的音叉可以用来演示**声的共振**。
把它们放在相隔不远的木制共鸣箱上。
让两个木箱的开口彼此相对（图83）。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
用小锤轻敲一只音叉的一个臂。
不久，另一只音叉也开始发声。
第一只音叉发出的声波，对另一只施加周期性的力。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
两只音叉的固有频率相同，所以另一只可以产生较大的振动响应。
若两只音叉的固有频率不同，响应强弱取决于频率相差多少。
外力频率落在接收音叉的狭窄共振频带之外时，响应会弱得多。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
在原来相同的任一音叉上固定一个轻金属夹。
金属夹会改变这只音叉的固有频率，使两只音叉可能失谐。
失谐足够大时，响应会减弱，也可能听不到声音。

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
音叉的振动阻尼较小，所以共振曲线比较尖锐。
这与第14节的讨论一致。

observed.title: 44. Sound Resonance

paragraphs.text:
Sounding objects can vibrate freely.
An external periodic force can drive them.
If the force's frequency is near their natural frequency, resonance can greatly boost the response.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Two identical tuning forks demonstrate **sound resonance**.
Set them a short distance apart on wooden resonance boxes.
Let the box openings face each other (Figure 83).

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Tap one arm of one fork with a small hammer.
The other fork soon begins to sound as well.
Sound waves from the first apply a periodic force to it.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Their matching natural frequencies allow a large response.
The response depends on the frequency difference.
Outside the receiving fork's narrow resonance band, it is much weaker.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Attach a light metal clip to either identical fork.
This shifts its natural frequency and can detune the pair.
With enough detuning, the response may become inaudible.

geometry.fontFamily: "Songti SC", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif

paragraphs.text:
Tuning forks have little damping, so their resonance curve is sharp.
This is the behavior discussed in Section 14.
